# `golden/ingest/` — the ingest fixture set (TASK-151)

Fixtures for the upload/paste ingest pipeline: the magic-byte sniff, the
header dimension read, the pre-decode pixel guard, the HEIC transcode and the
EXIF/XMP/GPS strip.

They are **committed**, read from disk by the tests, and generated by
[`generate.mjs`](./generate.mjs), which is run **by hand** and never at test
time. A fixture generated at test time can drift with its generator and still
agree with it — the same vacuous agreement `T-SEC-032e` exists to prevent.

Load them through [`index.ts`](./index.ts). Never `readFileSync` one directly:
one fixture is deliberately absent and the loader is what makes that fail
loudly instead of silently.

## Licence and provenance

Every file here was generated by `generate.mjs` in this repository. **Nothing
is third-party**, nothing was downloaded, and no photograph of a real place or
person is included. They are covered by the repository's MIT `LICENSE` and
carry no obligation for `npm run check:licences` to record.

The one exception is `heic-with-gps.heic`, which is **not present** — see the
blocker below. When it arrives it will be an owner-supplied photograph; record
its provenance in this section at that time.

## The set

| File                                   | Sniffs as | Declared type as handed to the pipeline | What it is for                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `control-screenshot.png`               | `png`     | `image/png`                             | The clean 1179×2556 control. The laptop/web capture path's output.                      |
| `control-screenshot-with-metadata.png` | `png`     | `image/png`                             | Carries `eXIf` (a real GPS-bearing TIFF block), `tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt`, `tIME`.         |
| `clipboard-blob.png`                   | `png`     | `image/png`                             | The pasted-bytes input: a 1170×2532 PNG, no filename, no metadata.                      |
| `control-photo.jpeg`                   | `jpeg`    | `image/jpeg`                            | Clean 2048×1536 JPEG control.                                                           |
| `control-photo-with-gps.jpeg`          | `jpeg`    | `image/jpeg`                            | APP1 EXIF + GPS IFD, APP13 IPTC, `COM` — **and an APP2 ICC profile that must survive**. |
| `heic-header.heic`                     | `heic`    | `image/heic`                            | A well-formed HEIC header at screenshot size.                                           |
| `heic-header.heic` _(same bytes)_      | `heic`    | **`application/octet-stream`**          | The iOS Safari case. Exposed as `heicAsOctetStream`.                                    |
| `heic-truncated.heic`                  | `heic`    | `image/heic`                            | Header intact, image data cut off. Decodes → `IMAGE_DECODE_FAILED`.                     |
| `heic-oversize.heic`                   | `heic`    | `image/heic`                            | Declares 8000×6000 (48.0 MP), over the 25 MP budget.                                    |
| `lying-blob.pdf`                       | _(none)_  | **`image/png`**                         | The lying-client case: a genuine PDF claiming to be an image.                           |
| `heic-with-gps.heic`                   | `heic`    | `application/octet-stream`              | **ABSENT — blocked.** See below.                                                        |

`declaredContentType` is recorded in the manifest **so a test can hand a lie to
the pipeline and assert the pipeline ignored it**. It is never an input to a
decision: format is decided by sniffed magic bytes only.

Two `ispe` boxes appear in every HEIC stub, **the small one first**. A real
iPhone file carries several (thumbnail, depth/auxiliary images, one per burst
frame) and the first is frequently the thumbnail, so a header reader that took
the first match would report a fraction of a megapixel and wave a 48 MP master
straight past the pixel guard — while passing every single-`ispe` fixture on
the way. `T-IMG-013g` is what makes that falsifiable.

## What the `.heic` stubs are, and are not

They are **container-accurate headers**: a real ISO-BMFF `ftyp` box with a
HEIF-family brand list, and a real `meta` → `iprp` → `ipco` → `ispe` tree. That
is enough to exercise the sniff, the dimension read, the pixel guard and — for
`heic-truncated.heic` — a **real `heic-convert` decode failure**, offline, with
nothing injected.

They contain **no decodable HEVC image item**, because this repository cannot
produce one: `T-DEP-002` forbids a HEIC **encoder** anywhere in the dependency
tree (patent exposure and a GPL licence floor). So no fixture here can assert a
successful real decode, or a real EXIF strip on real HEIC.

## 🛑 The blocker: `heic-with-gps.heic`

**Requested from the owner; not yet supplied. Two tests are RED because of it,
and that is the correct state of the world.**

Required: a real HEIC photograph taken on the owner's phone, delivered
**unedited** — not re-exported, not opened in a photo editor, not stripped —
still carrying its original EXIF including a GPS IFD (`GPSLatitude`,
`GPSLongitude`) and the device model.

Nothing in this repository substitutes for it:

1. **A synthetic HEIC is not evidence.** It would prove that our writer and our
   reader agree, not that the stripper survives what an iPhone actually writes.
2. **A GPS-bearing JPEG is not a substitute.** HEIC is the format that carries
   location in through the iOS camera-roll **file-upload** path; PNG and JPEG
   screenshots do not.
3. **The paste path cannot exercise it.** WebKit strips EXIF on
   `navigator.clipboard.read()` but **not** on file upload, so a pasted fixture
   passes vacuously whatever our code does. `T-SEC-033f` drives the **upload**
   path deliberately.

The two red tests are `T-SEC-033e` and `T-SEC-033f` in
`tests/extraction/ingestFixturesBlocked.spec.ts`. They fail with a
`MissingIngestFixtureError` naming the file and this requirement. **Do not skip
them and do not fabricate the file**: a skipped test is indistinguishable from
a passing one in a green run, and this is a privacy control (REQ-078,
`specs/security.md` §4.2).

To fix: drop the file at `tests/fixtures/golden/ingest/heic-with-gps.heic`.
Nothing else changes.
